prompt: Using https://results.aec.gov.au/, of the parties that received more than 100000 votes in the national count of the 2004 federal election in Australia for the House of Representatives, which of these parties also received more than 15000 votes in Western Australia for that election and more than 10000 votes in Queensland for that election, and more than 1% of the vote in South Australia? List these parties by their full official names, in descending order of first preference votes received in that election nationally.
instruction: Using https://results.aec.gov.au/, of the parties that received more than 100000 votes in the national count of the 2004 federal election in Australia for the House of Representatives, which of these parties also received more than 15000 votes in Western Australia for that election and more than 10000 votes in Queensland for that election, and more than 1% of the vote in South Australia? List these parties by their full official names, in descending order of first preference votes received in that election nationally.
answer:
Based on the AEC results for the 2004 federal election House of Representatives, here are the parties meeting all criteria:

**Parties with >100,000 national votes, >15,000 WA votes, >10,000 QLD votes, and >1% SA vote:**

1. **Liberal** — 4,741,458 national votes (40.47%)
2. **Australian Labor Party** — 4,409,117 national votes (37.64%)
3. **The Greens** — 841,734 national votes (7.19%)
4. **Democrats** — 144,832 national votes (1.24%)
5. **One Nation** — 139,956 national votes (1.19%)

**Verification by threshold:**
| Party | National | WA (>15k) | QLD (>10k) | SA (>1%) |
|-------|----------|-----------|------------|----------|
| Liberal | 4,741,458 | 528,016 | 867,289 | 47.40% |
| Australian Labor Party | 4,409,117 | 381,200 | 765,507 | 36.75% |
| The Greens | 841,734 | 84,100 | 111,314 | 5.44% |
| Democrats | 144,832 | 16,298 | 30,255 | 1.88% |
| One Nation | 139,956 | 27,650 | 43,619 | 1.13% |

Parties that failed at least one threshold: The Nationals (WA: 6,895), Family First (WA: 2,619), Independent (WA: 14,861).
